title: Copy a selected table before changing it
summary: Make your intended copy explicit when you want to edit a subset independently. This keeps the original table easier to reason about.
introduction: Make your intended copy explicit when you want to edit a subset independently. This keeps the original table easier to reason about. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Explain copy a selected table before changing it
Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: Make your intended copy explicit when you want to edit a subset independently. This keeps the original table easier to reason about.

blocks.code:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({
    "name": ["Asha", "Ben", "Cara"],
    "score": [8, 6, 9],
    "team": ["red", "blue", "red"]
})

selected = df.loc[df["team"] == "red"].copy()
selected["score"] = 0
print(df["score"].tolist())
blocks.title: Copy a selected table before changing it

blocks.text: The original scores remain [8, 6, 9]. The change applies to the copied subset.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Avoid chained assignment; use clear loc assignment or an explicit copy.
